pr.title: fix: handle web Response in auto HEAD route
pr.author: RubenPari

title: fastify#7139 Review Graph
summary: Fixes #7113: the auto-exposed HEAD route answered 500 when the GET handler sent a web Response, because the HEAD onSend hook runs before onSendEnd unwraps the Response and fell through to Buffer.byteLength. The hook gains a Response branch that cancels the body and hands onSendEnd a body-less Response with the same status and headers, passing null/used/locked bodies through unchanged. A second commit routes all HEAD stream-error logs through a new LogController#headStreamError. Three findings from the review (all Low/Nit).
note: Code read at head 3f3bd4d59b vs base ce41dc0fbb. Docs left out as a node: docs/Reference/Server.md (+1 row in the LogController method table, line 459). No generated files. No screenshots: library PR with no visible surface (headRouteOnSendHandler and onSendEnd are the nodes a captured HEAD/GET inject exchange would evidence). Reviewed while open; local tests not run, and CI had only run the label check on this head.

modeNotes.before: Base: a Response payload reaches Buffer.byteLength and throws; HEAD stream errors log via reply.log.error unconditionally.
modeNotes.after: Head: Response branch cancels the body and passes a body-less Response; stream errors go through LogController#headStreamError.

nodes.name: auto-HEAD registration
bullets: Registers HEAD for every GET route
nodes.summary: When exposeHeadRoute is on and the GET route has no explicit HEAD handler, route.js registers a HEAD route whose onSend list ends with headRouteOnSendHandler.

nodes.name: parseHeadOnSendHandlers
bullets: Appends the HEAD hook after user hooks
nodes.summary: Builds the HEAD route's onSend list: user-supplied onSend hooks first, headRouteOnSendHandler last, so the hook always sees the final payload.

nodes.name: headRouteOnSendHandler
bullets: Strips the body for auto-HEAD replies
New branch for a web Response payload
nodes.summary: The last onSend hook on an auto-HEAD route. It branches on the payload: undefined, node stream (resume and drain), web stream (cancel), and now web Response; anything else gets a content-length from Buffer.byteLength. The Response branch cancels a readable body and passes on new Response(null, { status, headers }) so onSendEnd applies GET's status and headers with no body; a null, used or locked body is passed through unchanged so HEAD reproduces GET's error. All three stream-error loggers now call LogController#headStreamError.
changes: Added Response branch (lines 32-45) using the same [object Response] tag check as reply.js
Pass-through when body is null, bodyUsed, or body.locked
reply.log.error(...) replaced by reply.server[kLogController].headStreamError(err, req, reply) in both stream branches and the new branch
facts: onSend phase, before onSendEnd unwraps a Response
last onSend hook on the HEAD route

nodes.summary: Four new integration tests: HEAD mirrors a 201 Response's status, x-demo and content-type with an empty body (:99); the body stream is cancelled with the HEAD reason (:122); a locked body gives 500 on GET and HEAD (:148); a cancel() error is logged at level 50 with the HEAD message (:172).

nodes.name: headStreamError
nodes.summary: A new public LogController method with the controller's shared error signature (error, request, reply, metadata). It returns early when request logging is disabled, else logs at error level with the message the old inline call used. Users who subclass LogController via the logController option can override it. Added in the refactor commit after a maintainer asked for logController instead of reply.log.
facts: 'Error on Stream found for HEAD route'

nodes.summary: Shared guard used by every error-logging method. Returns disableRequestLogging, or calls it with the request when it is a function.

nodes.name: logger.test.js
nodes.summary: Three unit tests mirroring the existing serializerError trio: no log when disableRequestLogging is true or a function returning true; logs the HEAD message with the error when enabled.

nodes.name: logger.tst.ts
nodes.summary: One tstyche assertion that headStreamError is callable with an Error, a FastifyRequest and a FastifyReply.

nodes.name: onSendEnd
bullets: Now receives a body-less Response on HEAD
nodes.summary: Unchanged code, but for HEAD it now receives either the original Response (null/used/locked body) or the hook's body-less copy. It applies payload.status and every header, throws FST_ERR_REP_RESPONSE_BODY_CONSUMED for a used body, then treats the null body as an empty reply; for HEAD it does not overwrite content-length (reply.js:657-658).

nodes.name: sendWebStream
nodes.summary: Reached on HEAD only through the pass-through of a locked body: throws FST_ERR_REP_READABLE_STREAM_LOCKED, which is the 500 the locked-body test asserts on both GET and HEAD.

nodes.name: Response
nodes.summary: The hook builds a body-less Response from the original's status and headers. Verified with node -e on Node 24: the copy keeps multiple set-cookie values and a user-set content-length, drops statusText, and the constructor only accepts status 200-599.

nodes.name: ReadableStream#cancel
nodes.summary: Called on payload (web stream branch) and payload.body (Response branch) with the reason 'Stream cancelled by HEAD route'; a rejection goes to headStreamError.

nodes.name: Buffer.byteLength
bullets: No longer reached by a Response
nodes.summary: The fallback branch sizes string/Buffer payloads. A Response reached it before the fix and threw ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE, which surfaced as the 500.

nodes.name: reply.log
nodes.summary: Before the PR the hook called reply.log.error directly; after it, only LogController#headStreamError writes to it.

nodes.name: disableRequestLogging
bullets: Now also silences HEAD stream errors
nodes.summary: The option isLogDisabled reads. Because headStreamError is guarded, HEAD stream-error lines are now suppressed when this is true — before the PR they were logged unconditionally.

edges.label: headStreamError(err, req, reply)
edges.detail: All three stream-error paths (node stream 'error', web stream cancel rejection, Response body cancel rejection) now call the LogController via reply.server[kLogController], the same access every other lib/ call site uses.

edges.label: reply.log.error(...)
edges.detail: The base logged stream errors inline with reply.log.error({ err }, 'Error on Stream found for HEAD route'), with no disableRequestLogging guard.

edges.label: isLogDisabled(request)
edges.detail: Early return when request logging is disabled — the behaviour change for the two pre-existing stream branches.

edges.label: reply.log.error({ err })
edges.detail: Same level and message as the removed inline call.

edges.label: body.cancel('Stream cancelled…')
edges.detail: New call for the Response branch (line 40); the web-stream branch's payload.cancel at line 25 is unchanged.

edges.label: new Response(null, {…})
edges.detail: Builds the body-less replacement passed to done(); the original's status and Headers object are copied.

edges.label: done(null, Response) → onSendEnd
edges.detail: The hook used to finish with done(null, null) for every handled payload; for a Response it now hands a Response (original or body-less copy) on to onSendEnd, which unwraps it exactly as for GET.

edges.label: sendWebStream(payload, …)
edges.detail: Reached on HEAD only when a locked body is passed through; throws FST_ERR_REP_READABLE_STREAM_LOCKED.

edges.label: declares headStreamError
edges.detail: The d.ts adds headStreamError(err, request, reply) to the LogController interface so TypeScript overrides type-check.

findings.title: Null-body and used-body pass-through, and header parity, untested
findings.text: Of the pass-through condition body === null || bodyUsed || body.locked (head-route.js:36), only the locked arm is tested (:148); the other two could be deleted without a failure. No new test asserts content-length or a multi-valued header on HEAD. Add a null-body 204 case, a consumed-body case (500 FST_ERR_REP_RESPONSE_BODY_CONSUMED on both), and extend :99 with content-length and two set-cookie values.

findings.title: New public LogController method and a logging behaviour change, not in the PR body
findings.text: The refactor commit adds an overridable LogController#headStreamError (types + docs) and routes the two pre-existing HEAD stream branches through it, so their error line is now suppressed under disableRequestLogging. Consistent with the controller's convention, but the PR body still describes only head-route.js; add a line so release notes and the 5.x backport (the issue says 5.x is affected) account for it.
